failure_summary.description: A 'his drama' clue that gives a foreign-language title was answered with the quoted title ('En folkefiende') instead of the creator. Rule 1 already says the 'his/her/this [work]' form asks for the person.

'One of the buildings at this British site is named for X' was answered with the named part ('Devereux Tower') instead of the containing site. No rule covers part-to-whole clues, and the answer echoed a clue name.
Extra qualifiers were added to the bare generic noun: 'NFL football' for 'this sport', and 'speech balloon' for a 'term for' clue. The qualifier restates the clue or adds a league/brand.
A middle-initial expansion ('George H. W. Bush') was used when the clue itself writes the short form 'George Bush'.

patch.reasoning: Three of the five misses are over-specific answers. Two are the wrong slot: the quoted work instead of its creator, and the named part instead of its containing site. The other three have the right entity in the wrong form: extra qualifiers on a bare noun, and an expanded name. The earlier mandatory-template edits in this epoch were rejected and cost score, so these four edits are short and keyed to visible clue features. Two cover the creator and the container, one covers bare generic nouns, and one covers the name form copied from the clue. None touches Rule 3, which drives the stable passes.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content: - 'His/her/its <work>' clues (a quoted title, a foreign-language title, a translation, a described work) ask for the CREATOR or OWNER, never the work, its title or its translation. '"<Title in another language>" is the Norwegian title of his 1882 drama' -> the dramatist. If your candidate is the title or work already quoted in the clue, switch to the person who made it.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content: - 'One of the buildings / wings / rooms / towers at this site (castle, campus, museum, prison)', especially with 'named for <person>' or 'held there', asks for the WHOLE that contains the part: the site itself. The part and the person it is named for are anchors. Reject a candidate that contains a name from the clue ('<Person> Tower', '<Person> Wing') and answer with the containing place.

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content: - 'This sport / game / animal / food / instrument' and 'Term for ...' clues want the BARE generic name. Add no league, brand, country or sport prefix, and no qualifier that merely restates the clue's own description. Ball measurements for 'this sport' -> 'Football', not 'NFL football'. 'Term for the circle enclosing a character's dialogue' -> 'Balloon', not 'speech balloon', because 'speech' just restates 'dialogue'. Keep a modifier only when it is part of the standard term and the bare noun alone would not name the thing ('Charley horse').

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content: - Name form: when the clue itself writes the person's name in short form ('George Bush won the election'), copy that short form. Do not expand it with middle initials or extra given names ('George H. W. Bush'). Drop middle initials by default unless a verbatim archive answer in the context (Rule 3) includes them.
